intro.text: A huge Horneater bridgeman in Sadeas's Bridge Four, sent to the bridge crews after serving the highprince as a cook.
A Horneater member of Bridge Four, its cook and quartermaster, who can see spren and refuses to fight.
Lunamor, better known as Rock, is an Unkalaki cook and Windrunner squire in Bridge Four. His full name is a poem about a remarkable stone his father found the day before he was born.
Lunamor, better known as Rock, is an Unkalaki cook and former member of Bridge Four, who has gone home to the Horneater Peaks with his family.

items.text: Rock was born in the Horneater Peaks, the fourth son of his family, and was trained with spear and bow. He loved cooking from early on, making bread with his mother. As a child he built snow forts with Tuaka, whose forts he admits were always best. They married and had six children before he left the Peaks.

Rock came to the Shattered Plains with his nuatoma, Kef'ha, who hoped to win Shards for their people. Kef'ha challenged Torol Sadeas to a duel for his Plate and was killed, and Rock and the rest of the entourage became Sadeas's servants.
Sadeas used Rock as a cook. Angry over his nuatoma's death, Rock served him one meal with chull dung in every dish, and was sent to the bridge crews, landing in Bridge Four.

Rock had been a bridgeman for months when Kaladin became bridgeleader. He laughed at Kaladin's promise that they would lose no more men, and was surprised when Kaladin took his place at the front of the bridge. Afterwards Rock carried the wounded Dabbid to shelter and went back with Teft for Leyten.

Rock shared his food with the wounded and, seeing Syl, helped gather knobweed sap. On chasm duty he drew Dunny into the crew's talk. With the money from the sap, he and Kaladin bought a cauldron, and Rock cooked a stew the whole crew shared; after that most of them began training with Kaladin.
When Kaladin's side carry saved every man in Bridge Four but cost Sadeas the assault, Rock stepped up to defend him, but was ordered aside and watched him beaten.

After Kaladin was strung up in a highstorm, Rock was the first out of the barracks to check on him, dismayed to find him seemingly dead and then delighted that he lived, and called the others to help cut him down.

While Kaladin recovered, Rock led Bridge Four, though the men called him squadleader and Kaladin captain. To thank him for his cooking, the crew bought him a razor, which brought him to tears, and he began shaving them all.
When Kaladin began training the crew to escape, Rock alone refused to learn the spear and became their official cook.

Rock helped hold Kaladin down when he had visions during a highstorm, and revealed that Sigzil was a Worldsinger. He explained to Kaladin why he would not fight, and instead led Lopen, Dabbid and Shen in collecting salvage while the others trained.
Rock was there when Dunny died on a plateau run, and helped save wounded men from other crews.
On chasm duty, Rock used a bow to fix a pouch of found spheres under a bridge, to be collected on the next run, insisting he would shoot bridges but never use the weapon in battle.
Rock kept drilling the crew in bridge carries while Kaladin learned about the Knights Radiant from Teft.

At the Tower, Rock wore Leyten's carapace armour with the rest of Bridge Four. When Sadeas betrayed Dalinar, Rock agreed with Kaladin to go back for Dalinar's men, saw Kaladin save Adolin and Dalinar, and helped carry the bridge home, where Dalinar traded Oathbringer for the bridgemen's lives.
Afterwards Rock cooked a nightly stew for Bridge Four, and joined the crew in testing the limits of Kaladin's powers.

Freed, Rock was made a lieutenant and Bridge Four's quartermaster, with Lopen as his second. Though he had no slave brand to hide, he took the crew's forehead tattoo with the rest, and wore the Cobalt Guard uniform with the Bridge Four patch as they became Dalinar's guard.

Kaladin had Rock train men from the other bridge crews as cooks. In the chasms, Rock offered to build Syl a shrine, saw spren pulling stones to the walls as they tested Kaladin's powers, and sparred with Kaladin, though he still would not fight in battle.
Hobber, who had lost the use of his legs fighting the Assassin in White, joined Rock's support crew alongside Lopen and Dabbid. When Renarin joined Bridge Four, he helped Rock with the dishes.

Over drinks, Rock told the crew of his homeland and its gods, and of the hot springs that connect the Peaks to them, but refused to explain how he saw spren. Sigzil was startled when Rock named a god, Lunu'anaki, who was the very man Sigzil had trained under as a Worldsinger.

While Kaladin was imprisoned, Rock kept a stew going for him. He joined the expedition to Narak, defending Shen, now known as Rlain, to Dalinar as one of Bridge Four, escorted Shallan to find the Oathgate, and greeted Kaladin after he defeated the Assassin in White.
After the battle, several bridgemen began to glow with Stormlight.

When Kaladin took Bridge Four to the Shattered Plains to practise with Stormlight, Rock cooked and quietly recited the First Ideal. He told Renarin he could never see Renarin's spren, and urged him to talk to Rlain. Skar taught him to draw in Stormlight, and Rock offered infused gems to the honorspren watching them.

Investigating smoke on the Plains, Bridge Four found a caravan attacked by Voidbringers, and among the survivors were Rock's wife, Song, and their six children. Song told him something was terribly wrong in the Peaks. Rock carried the bridge one last time on the way back, as Bridge Four would fly from then on.

Rock and Kaladin found Teft in a firemoss den and brought him home with promises of help. Rock was among the bridgemen attacked by agents of the Diagram trying to steal Jezrien's Honorblade, which the crew was passing between them.

After Bridge Four retook Urithiru from a listener strike, they led troops through the Oathgate to Thaylen City. There Rock killed Amaram, now bonded to Yelig-nar, with two arrows from a Shardbow, through the head and the gemheart, to save Kaladin. Breaking his vow against violence shook him, and Kaladin and Teft consoled him.

A year on, Rock joined the Fourth Bridge expedition to evacuate Hearthstone, passing Kaladin spears against the Heavenly Ones and warning others of the Pursuer. With his daughter Cord, he guarded Dalinar while he held open Honor's Perpendicularity.

Rock then left for the Horneater Peaks with his wife and younger children, telling Kaladin he had broken his people's ways and must face justice. He asked for and received Kaladin's blessing, and Skar and Drehy flew with them as an honour guard. He told Kaladin they would not meet again in this life.
When Skar and Drehy came back, they told Kaladin that Rock would not be returning.

appearance.text: He has tan skin and deep red hair, cropped close and shaved up the centre of his head. When he can, he shaves his chin and lip but leaves long red-blond muttonchop sideburns.
Like the rest of Bridge Four, he has the crew's glyphs tattooed on his forehead.
A huge man nearly seven feet tall, a few inches taller than Kaladin and almost twice as broad.

personality.text: He is very proud of his cooking and will let no one alter his stew. He is deeply respectful of spren, to Syl's delight and Kaladin's annoyance.
Rock refuses to fight, because Unkalaki do not hold soldiering in esteem, though he is skilled with the bow.
Rock is openly emotional, as quick to laugh as to grieve, and bridgemen often come to him for advice. He is fiercely loyal to those who trust him, and was among the first to follow Kaladin.
